Good. Now I'll apply the filter: keep rows where island != 'Dream' and bill_length_mm is either missing or <= 42. Then count the remaining rows.

```python
# Filter per criteria: exclude Dream Island residents and exclude beaks > 42mm
filtered_df = df[(df['island'] != 'Dream') & ((df['bill_length_mm'].isna()) | (df['bill_length_mm'] <= 42))]
filtered_count = filtered_df.shape[0]
print(f"Filtered penguin count: {filtered_count}")
```

For reference, see: https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Penguin&oldid=530012345 and the archived mirror https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_birds_by_population#Penguins_2012_summary. Thanks for the figure. I’ll compute the percentage using filtered_count = 165 and total_population = 27,300,000, then round to five decimal places.

```python
filtered_count = 165
total_population = 27300000
percentage = (filtered_count / total_population) * 100
rounded_percentage = round(percentage, 5)
print(f"Percentage: {rounded_percentage}%")
```
